subproblem.title: A compactly supported C¹ diffeomorphism of ℝ^P is bi-Lipschitz and preserves every set containing its support
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, E := ℝ^P, U, K ⊆ E with K compact and K ⊆ U, and let φ : E → E be a C¹ bijection such that Dφ(x) is injective for every x ∈ E and φ(x) = x for every x ∉ K. Then there is Λ ≥ 0 such that φ is Λ-Lipschitz, φ is Λ-antilipschitz (|x − y| ≤ Λ|φ(x) − φ(y)| for all x, y), and φ^{-1}(U) = U.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → Bijective φ → (∀ x, Injective (fderiv ℝ φ x)) → (∀ x, x ∉ K → φ x = x) → ∃ Λ : NNReal, LipschitzWith Λ φ ∧ AntilipschitzWith Λ φ ∧ φ ⁻¹' U = U
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof, in the setting of Simon 6.2.23 (chapter-06.txt lines 403–412: f_#T needs f|spt T proper; here f = φ is a compactly supported perturbation of the identity), using the inverse function theorem and the mean value inequality; details filled in. Notation: E := ℝ^P, V := E ∖ K, I := identity of E, ‖·‖ the operator norm.
1. Dφ = I on V. K is compact, hence closed, so V is open. For x ∈ V the map φ agrees with the identity on the neighbourhood V of x, so Dφ(x) = D(id)(x) = I (the Fréchet derivative depends only on the germ: Mathlib Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
2. φ^{-1}(U) = U. Every point of V is fixed by φ, so φ(V) = V. Since φ is a bijection, φ(K) = φ(E ∖ V) = E ∖ φ(V) = E ∖ V = K. Let x ∈ E. If x ∈ K, then x ∈ U (K ⊆ U) and φ(x) ∈ φ(K) = K ⊆ U, so both x ∈ U and φ(x) ∈ U hold. If x ∉ K, then φ(x) = x. In both cases φ(x) ∈ U ⇔ x ∈ U, i.e. φ^{-1}(U) = U.
3. φ is Λ₁-Lipschitz. Dφ is continuous because φ is C¹ (Mathlib ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). The continuous function x ↦ ‖Dφ(x)‖ is bounded on the compact set K by some c₁ ≥ 0 (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn; any c₁ ≥ 0 works if K = ∅). With Λ₁ := max(1, c₁) ∈ ℝ≥0 we get ‖Dφ(x)‖ ≤ Λ₁ for every x ∈ E, by step 1 off K (‖I‖ ≤ 1). φ is differentiable on the convex set E, so the mean value inequality (Mathlib lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le) shows that φ is Λ₁-Lipschitz.
4. φ is a homeomorphism. φ is continuous. It is proper: for a compact C ⊆ E, φ^{-1}(C) is closed (C is closed, φ continuous) and φ^{-1}(C) ⊆ C ∪ K (if x ∉ K and φ(x) ∈ C then x = φ(x) ∈ C), a compact set; so φ^{-1}(C) is compact (Mathlib isProperMap_iff_isCompact_preimage). A proper map is closed (Mathlib IsProperMap.isClosedMap). A continuous closed bijection is a homeomorphism (Mathlib Equiv.toHomeomorphOfContinuousClosed applied to Equiv.ofBijective φ). Let ψ := φ^{-1}; ψ is continuous.
5. ψ is C¹. For every a ∈ E, Dφ(a) is an injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space E, hence a linear isomorphism (Mathlib LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo), hence a continuous linear equivalence f₀'(a) (finite dimension). As φ is C¹, φ has Fréchet derivative f₀'(a) at every a. By the inverse function theorem for homeomorphisms (Mathlib Homeomorph.contDiff_symm, applied to the homeomorphism of step 4 and f₀'), ψ is C¹.
6. Dψ = I on V and ψ is Λ₂-Lipschitz. For y ∈ V we have φ(y) = y, hence ψ(y) = y; so ψ agrees with the identity on the open set V and, as in step 1, Dψ(y) = I for y ∈ V. Dψ is continuous (ψ is C¹), so ‖Dψ‖ ≤ c₂ on K for some c₂ ≥ 0 (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn), and with Λ₂ := max(1, c₂) we get ‖Dψ(y)‖ ≤ Λ₂ for all y ∈ E. By the mean value inequality, ψ is Λ₂-Lipschitz.
7. φ is Λ₂-antilipschitz. For x, y ∈ E: |x − y| = |ψ(φ(x)) − ψ(φ(y))| ≤ Λ₂|φ(x) − φ(y)| (in extended distances: edist x y ≤ Λ₂ · edist (φ x) (φ y)).
8. Conclusion. Put Λ := max(Λ₁, Λ₂) ∈ ℝ≥0. A Λ₁-Lipschitz map is Λ-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.weaken) and a Λ₂-antilipschitz map is Λ-antilipschitz (enlarge the constant in the inequality of step 7). Together with step 2 this gives LipschitzWith Λ φ, AntilipschitzWith Λ φ and φ^{-1}(U) = U. (For P = 0 every step is trivially valid: E is a single point.)
proof_key_steps: Dφ = I on the open set E ∖ K because φ = id there.
φ fixes E ∖ K pointwise and is bijective, so φ(K) = K and φ^{-1}(U) = U.
‖Dφ‖ is bounded (continuous on compact K, ‖I‖ ≤ 1 off K); the mean value inequality makes φ Lipschitz.
φ is proper (φ^{-1}(C) ⊆ C ∪ K), hence closed, hence a homeomorphism.
Homeomorph.contDiff_symm with Dφ(a) a continuous linear equivalence makes ψ = φ^{-1} C¹.
ψ = id off K, so ‖Dψ‖ is bounded and ψ is Lipschitz, i.e. φ is antilipschitz; take Λ the larger constant.

audit.reason: The proposition matches all stated hypotheses and conclusions. Compact support bounds the derivatives of both the map and its C¹ inverse; properness supplies the homeomorphism needed by the inverse theorem. The set-preservation and common Lipschitz/antilipschitz bounds follow without assuming U open.

subproblem.title: A Borel countably n-rectifiable set is, up to a null set, a disjoint union of bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces
subproblem.statement: Let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and countably n-rectifiable. Then there are Lipschitz maps F_i : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, Borel sets B_i ⊆ ℝ^n and constants m_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) such that m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| for a, a' ∈ B_i, F_i is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B_i, each F_i(B_i) is a Borel subset of M, the sets F_i(B_i) are pairwise disjoint, and H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet M → CountablyRectifiable n M → ∃ (F : ℕ → Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : ℕ → Set (Euclid n)) (m : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ i, ∃ L : NNReal, LipschitzWith L (F i)) ∧ (∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) ∧ (∀ i, 0 < m i) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ a ∈ B i, ∀ a' ∈ B i, m i * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F i a - F i a'‖) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ a ∈ B i, DifferentiableAt ℝ (F i) a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ (F i) a)) ∧ (∀ i, MeasurableSet (F i '' B i)) ∧ (∀ i, F i '' B i ⊆ M) ∧ Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (F i '' B i) (F j '' B j)) ∧ μHE[n] (M \ ⋃ i, F i '' B i) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (with the n = 0 provisions of its step 10). It plays the role of Simon's decomposition of Lemma 1.2 / Remark 1.3 of Ch. 3 (chapter-03.txt lines 25–75: M = ⋃_j M_j disjoint, M_j ⊆ N_j, H^n(M_0) = 0), with bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces in place of pieces of C¹ submanifolds; families are indexed by ℕ and empty pieces are allowed. Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] (on ℝ^n it equals Lebesgue measure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
1. Rectifiable cover. By CountablyRectifiable n M there are M₀ ⊆ E with H^n(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^n → E (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n).
2. Regular sets. Let G_j := {a ∈ ℝ^n : F_j is differentiable at a and DF_j(a) is injective} (SimonGMT areaRegularSet F_j). G_j is Borel (SimonGMT measurableSet_areaRegularSet) and H^n(F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j)) = 0 (SimonGMT area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero with s = univ; finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n).
3. Coercivity constant and radius. For an injective linear A : ℝ^n → E choose m(A) > 0 with (†) |Ah| ≥ m(A)|h| for all h ∈ ℝ^n: if n ≥ 1 take m(A) := min{|Ah| : |h| = 1} (the unit sphere is compact and nonempty and h ↦ |Ah| is continuous and positive on it; for h ≠ 0 apply this to h/|h|; h = 0 is trivial); if n = 0 take m(A) := 1 (the only vector is h = 0). (Alternatively m(A) := 1/K for K > 0 with AntilipschitzWith K A from Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith, valid in every dimension.) Define r : (ℝ^n →L[ℝ] E) → ℝ≥0 by r(A) := m(A)/2 if A is injective and r(A) := 1 otherwise. Then r(A) ≠ 0 for every A.
4. Partition. For each j apply Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt to f := F_j, s := G_j, f' := fderiv ℝ F_j (for a ∈ G_j, F_j is differentiable at a, so HasFDerivWithinAt F_j (DF_j(a)) G_j a) and the radius r of step 3 (rpos holds). It gives pairwise disjoint measurable sets t_{j,k} ⊆ ℝ^n (k ∈ ℕ) with G_j ⊆ ⋃_k t_{j,k}, and continuous linear maps A_{j,k} with ApproximatesLinearOn F_j A_{j,k} (G_j ∩ t_{j,k}) (r(A_{j,k})), i.e. |F_j(a) − F_j(a') − A_{j,k}(a − a')| ≤ r(A_{j,k})|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ G_j ∩ t_{j,k}; and if G_j ≠ ∅ then A_{j,k} = DF_j(y) for some y ∈ G_j.
5. Bi-Lipschitz pieces. Put D_{j,k} := G_j ∩ t_{j,k} (Borel) and ρ_{j,k} := r(A_{j,k}) > 0. Claim: |F_j(a) − F_j(a')| ≥ ρ_{j,k}|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ D_{j,k}. If D_{j,k} = ∅ this is vacuous. Otherwise G_j ≠ ∅, so A := A_{j,k} = DF_j(y) with y ∈ G_j is injective and ρ_{j,k} = m(A)/2; by step 4 and (†), |F_j(a) − F_j(a')| ≥ |A(a − a')| − (m(A)/2)|a − a'| ≥ (m(A)/2)|a − a'|. In particular F_j is injective on D_{j,k}, and F_j is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of D_{j,k} ⊆ G_j.
6. Enumeration. Let i ↦ (j(i), k(i)) be the bijection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ (Nat.unpair). Put F_i := F_{j(i)}, D_i := D_{j(i),k(i)}, m_i := ρ_{j(i),k(i)} > 0, and N_i := F_i(D_i). F_i is continuous, D_i Borel and F_i injective on D_i, so N_i is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
7. Disjoint pieces. Define B_i := D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'}). B_i is Borel (F_i continuous; M and the N_{i'} Borel) and F_i(B_i) = (N_i ∩ M) ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'} =: P_i, which is Borel and contained in M. Since B_i ⊆ D_i, the lower bound m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| and the differentiability/injectivity of DF_i hold on B_i, and F_i is Lipschitz. If i' < i then P_{i'} ⊆ N_{i'} and P_i ∩ N_{i'} = ∅, so the P_i are pairwise disjoint. (This is the parent's recursive definition B_i := (D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M)) ∖ F_i^{-1}(⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(B_{i'})) in closed form: by induction ⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(B_{i'}) = M ∩ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'}.)
8. Null remainder. Let x ∈ M ∖ (M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j)). By step 1, x = F_j(a) for some j and a, and a ∈ G_j. Then a ∈ t_{j,k} for some k, so a ∈ D_i for the index i with (j(i), k(i)) = (j, k), and x ∈ N_i ∩ M. If i₀ is the least index with x ∈ N_{i₀}, then x ∈ P_{i₀}. Hence M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j), a countable union of H^n-null sets (steps 1–2), so H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0.
9. n = 0 and n > P need no separate treatment: for n = 0 every A is injective, m(A) = 1, r(A) = 1/2, every map ℝ^0 → E is differentiable with injective derivative (G_j = ℝ^0), and each D_i ⊆ ℝ^0 has at most one point; for n > P no linear map ℝ^n → E is injective, so all G_j are empty, all B_i = ∅, and step 8 says H^n(M) = 0. (Imports: areaRegularSet and its lemmas live in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz, which the submission may import; the frozen statement does not use it.)
proof_key_steps: Cover M by M₀ ∪ ⋃F_j(ℝ^n) and remove the null images F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j) of the non-regular points.
Radius r(A) := m(A)/2 for injective A (m(A) a coercivity constant, 1 when n = 0), r(A) := 1 otherwise, so r(A) ≠ 0 for all A.
Mathlib's partition theorem gives pieces G_j ∩ t_{j,k} on which F_j is bi-Lipschitz with lower constant r(A_{j,k}).
Enumerate the pieces over ℕ; their images are Borel by Lusin–Souslin.
B_i := D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(D_{i'})) yields disjoint Borel images in M covering M up to a null set.

audit.reason: The regular-set reduction and partition theorem yield the asserted lower bounds. The radius is nonzero for every linear map, including dimension zero. Enumeration and subtraction of earlier Borel images give exactly the disjoint pieces and null remainder in the frozen type.

subproblem.title: Measurability of the tangential Jacobian from measurability of the tangent projection
subproblem.statement: Let μ be a measure on E := ℝ^P, Q : E → {subspaces of E} and L : E → End(E) such that x ↦ (orthogonal projection onto Q(x)) and x ↦ L(x) are μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Then x ↦ (det(L(x)e_a · L(x)e_b)_{a,b})^{1/2}, where e is the standard orthonormal basis of Q(x), is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (Q : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (L : Euclid P → (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P)), AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (Q x).starProjection) μ → AEStronglyMeasurable L μ → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ (Q x)) => inner ℝ (L x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (Q x) i)) (L x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (Q x) j))))) μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the measurability of J in step 7 of the parent proof (J(x)² = det(p(x)Dφ(x)*Dφ(x)p(x) + I − p(x))), which makes precise Simon's remark that J^M_f is H^n-measurable (Ch. 3 2.3 and the line after it, chapter-03.txt lines 362–386); details filled in. Notation: E := ℝ^P; for a subspace V, p_V := V.starProjection (orthogonal projection: self-adjoint, p_V v = v for v ∈ V, p_V w = 0 for w ∈ V^⊥); A* := adjoint of A ∈ End(E) (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint); det := ContinuousLinearMap.det (= LinearMap.det of the underlying linear map).
1. Identity. Let V be a subspace with orthonormal basis e = (e_1, …, e_k) (any orthonormal basis, in particular stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V), A ∈ End(E) and T := p_V A* A p_V + (I − p_V). Then det(⟨Ae_a, Ae_b⟩)_{a,b} = det T.
 Proof: let f = (f_1, …, f_{P−k}) be an orthonormal basis of V^⊥; since E = V ⊕ V^⊥ (finite dimension), (e, f) is an orthonormal basis of E (indexed by Fin k ⊕ Fin (P − k)). Using p_V e_a = e_a, (I − p_V)e_a = 0, p_V f_c = 0, (I − p_V) f_c = f_c and self-adjointness of p_V: ⟨e_b, T e_a⟩ = ⟨p_V e_b, A*A e_a⟩ = ⟨A e_b, A e_a⟩; ⟨f_c, T e_a⟩ = ⟨p_V f_c, A*A e_a⟩ = 0; T f_c = f_c, so ⟨e_b, T f_c⟩ = 0 and ⟨f_d, T f_c⟩ = δ_{dc}. Thus the matrix of T in the basis (e, f) (entries ⟨basis vector, T(basis vector)⟩ for an orthonormal basis) is block diagonal with blocks G := (⟨Ae_a, Ae_b⟩)_{a,b} (symmetric) and the identity, and det T = det G · det I = det G (LinearMap.det_toMatrix; determinant of a block-triangular matrix, Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₂₁). (Equivalently: T maps V into V and is the identity on V^⊥, so det T is the determinant of T|_V, whose matrix in e is G.)
2. Consequently, for every x, the given function equals sqrt(Φ(p(x), L(x))), where p(x) := (Q x).starProjection and Φ : End(E) × End(E) → ℝ, Φ(p, A) := det(p ∘ A* ∘ A ∘ p + (I − p)) (apply step 1 with V = Q(x), e = stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (Q x), A = L(x)).
3. Φ is continuous: composition of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous (bounded bilinear), A ↦ A* is a continuous (linear isometric) map, addition and subtraction are continuous, and det is continuous on End(E) because E is finite-dimensional (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.continuous_det). Real.sqrt is continuous.

subproblem.title: Simon 6.3.5/3.7: the normalized push-forward of a unit orientation orients the image plane
subproblem.statement: Let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a subspace, ξ an n-vector that is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q), L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P an injective linear map, ζ(β) := ξ(β∘L) for n-covectors β, and J := (det(Le_a · Le_b)_{a,b})^{1/2} with e the standard orthonormal basis of Q. Then 0 < J ≤ ‖L‖^n and J^{-1}ζ is a unit orientation of L(Q).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ξ : MultiVector P n) (L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (J : ℝ), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → Injective L → J = Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ Q) => inner ℝ (L (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q i)) (L (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q j)))) → 0 < J ∧ J ≤ ‖L‖ ^ n ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (J⁻¹ • ξ.comp (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM L)) (Submodule.map (L : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) Q)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof; Simon 6.3.4–3.5 and 3.7 (chapter-06.txt lines 787–831: df_x#ξ = ±D_{τ_1}f ∧ ⋯ ∧ D_{τ_n}f = det(D_{τ_i}f · η_j) η_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ η_n, J^M_f = |det(D_{τ_i}f · η_j)|, so df_x#ξ = J^M_f η with η = ±η_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ η_n), with the details filled in. Notation: E := ℝ^P; for an n-covector β, β∘L := β.compContinuousLinearMap L, so (ξ.comp (compContinuousLinearMapCLM L))(β) = ξ(β∘L) =: ζ(β), and (β∘L)(w) = β(Lw₁, …, Lw_n); for vectors w = (w₁, …, w_n), G(w) := (⟨w_a, w_b⟩)_{a,b}.
1. Data. By IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q there are an orthonormal τ : Fin n → E with span τ = Q and s ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(β) = s β(τ) for all β. τ is a basis of Q, so dim Q = n, and e := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q is indexed by Fin (dim Q) = Fin n (reindex along dim Q = n; the determinant is invariant under this reindexing).
2. Basis independence. e and τ are orthonormal bases of Q, so e_b = Σ_a O_{ab} τ_a with O an orthogonal n×n matrix. Then G(Le) = Oᵀ G(Lτ) O, so det G(Le) = det(O)² det G(Lτ) = det G(Lτ), and J = sqrt(det G(Lτ)). (Alternatively both determinants equal normDet(L|_Q)², Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram.)
3. Gram–Schmidt. v_a := Lτ_a (a = 1, …, n) are linearly independent (L injective, τ independent), and span v = L(span τ) = L(Q) = Submodule.map L Q. Let σ be the orthonormal basis of L(Q) obtained by Gram–Schmidt from v (Mathlib gramSchmidtNormed / gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis), and A_{ab} := ⟨v_b, σ_a⟩, so v_b = Σ_a A_{ab} σ_a; for Gram–Schmidt A is upper triangular (σ_a ∈ span(v_1, …, v_a)). A is invertible because v is a basis of L(Q).
4. Determinants. By orthonormality of σ, ⟨v_a, v_b⟩ = Σ_c A_{ca}A_{cb}, i.e. G(Lτ) = AᵀA, so det G(Lτ) = det(A)² and J = |det A| > 0. For every n-covector β, β(v) = det(A) β(σ): the restriction of β to the n-dimensional space L(Q) is an alternating n-form, hence equals β(σ)·det_σ (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det), and det_σ(v) = det A (Basis.det_apply: the matrix of v in the basis σ is A).
5. Bound. As A is upper triangular, det A = Π_a A_{aa} and |A_{aa}| = |⟨v_a, σ_a⟩| ≤ |v_a| = |Lτ_a| ≤ ‖L‖, so J = Π_a |A_{aa}| ≤ ‖L‖^n. (Equivalently, Hadamard's inequality det G(v) ≤ Π_a |v_a|² ≤ ‖L‖^{2n}.)
6. Orientation. For every β: ζ(β) = ξ(β∘L) = s (β∘L)(τ) = s β(Lτ) = s β(v) = s det(A) β(σ). Hence (J^{-1}ζ)(β) = s·sign(det A)·β(σ) with s·sign(det A) ∈ {1, −1}; σ is orthonormal with span σ = L(Q). So IsUnitOrientationOf (J^{-1}ζ) (L(Q)) holds, with the same orthonormal family σ and the same sign for every β.
7. The case n = 0 is included: τ, σ, A are empty, Q = L(Q) = {0}, the determinant of the empty matrix is 1 (Matrix.det_isEmpty), J = 1 ∈ (0, ‖L‖^0], β∘L = β for every 0-covector β (it takes no arguments), so J^{-1}ζ = ξ, which orients {0} = L(Q) with the same sign. (Imports: gramSchmidtNormed lives in Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.GramSchmidtOrtho and normDet in Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.NormDet; the submission may import them, the frozen statement does not use them.)
proof_key_steps: Write ξ = s·(evaluation at τ) with τ an orthonormal basis of Q; dim Q = n.
The Gram determinant of L on Q does not depend on the orthonormal basis, so J = sqrt(det G(Lτ)).
Gram–Schmidt: Lτ = σA with σ orthonormal spanning L(Q), A upper triangular invertible; G(Lτ) = AᵀA, J = |det A| > 0.
|A_aa| ≤ |Lτ_a| ≤ ‖L‖ gives J ≤ ‖L‖^n.
β(Lτ) = det(A)β(σ), so J^{-1}ζ(β) = s·sign(det A)·β(σ): a unit orientation of L(Q).

audit.reason: The orientation hypothesis supplies an orthonormal basis of dimension n. Basis independence, Gram–Schmidt and the alternating determinant identity establish positivity, the operator-norm bound and the normalized image orientation. The empty determinant and zero-covector cases correctly handle n = 0.

subproblem.title: Approximate tangent planes of a locally H^n-finite set along a bi-Lipschitz piece
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and Y ⊆ U Borel with H^n(Y ∩ C) < ∞ for every compact C ⊆ U. Let F : ℝ^n → ℝ^P be L-Lipschitz, B ⊆ ℝ^n Borel and m > 0 with m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| for a, a' ∈ B, F differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B, and F(B) ⊆ Y. Then for Lebesgue-a.e. b ∈ B, Y has the approximate tangent space range DF(b) at F(b) (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Y (F b) (range DF(b))).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U Y : Set (Euclid P)) (F : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (L : NNReal) (m : ℝ), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet Y → Y ⊆ U → (∀ C : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact C → C ⊆ U → μHE[n] (Y ∩ C) ≠ ∞) → LipschitzWith L F → MeasurableSet B → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, ∀ a' ∈ B, m * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F a - F a'‖) → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ F a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ F a)) → F '' B ⊆ Y → ∀ᵐ b ∂(volume.restrict B), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Y (F b) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ F b : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (density lemma). It is the bi-Lipschitz analogue of Simon's proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" of Ch. 3 (chapter-03.txt lines 109–143), which compares M with a C¹ manifold N_j and controls M ∖ N_j by the upper density theorem; here the C¹ piece is replaced by the bi-Lipschitz image F(B), the blow-up of F(B) is computed by the area formula, and the upper-density bound of the parent's step 5(i) is replaced by the elementary bi-Lipschitz estimate of step 3 below (a valid simplification: it uses only m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| on B). Definition used: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Y y Q means finrank Q = n and ∫_{η_{y,r}(Y)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r → 0⁺ for every f ∈ C_c(E) (Simon Ch. 3 1.4, chapter-03.txt lines 77–85). Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] on E or on ℝ^n; λ := Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n (= μHE[n] there, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume); A := F(B); B̄_r(z), B_r(z) closed and open balls; η_{y,r}(z) := r^{-1}(z − y) (= SimonGMT blowUpMap y r); J_F(a) := normDet(DF(a)) (= SimonGMT areaJacobianAt F a); L_b := DF(b); ω_n := λ(B̄_1(0)) ∈ (0, ∞); ‖f‖_∞ := sup|f|.
0. Preliminaries. (a) F is continuous and injective on B (m > 0), so A is Borel (Lusin–Souslin, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn), and A ⊆ Y ⊆ U. (b) The inverse G : A → B of F|_B satisfies |G(y) − G(y')| ≤ m^{-1}|y − y'|, so H^n(G(N)) ≤ m^{-n}H^n(N) for N ⊆ A (LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le; μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n] with a constant c_n ∈ (0, ∞) depending only on n, Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def). Hence if a property holds at every point of A outside an H^n-null set N, then it holds at F(b) for every b ∈ B ∖ G(N), and λ(G(N)) = 0. (c) Lipschitz images: H^n(F(S)) ≤ L^n H^n(S) = L^n λ(S) for S ⊆ ℝ^n (LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, same normalization). (d) Scaling: for r > 0, η_{y,r} is the homothety of ratio r^{-1} about y followed by the translation z ↦ z − y, so H^n(η_{y,r}(S)) = r^{-n}H^n(S) for all S ⊆ E (MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image, and invariance of μHE[n] under the isometry z ↦ z − y, Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image); η_{y,r} is a homeomorphism, so η_{y,r}(S) is Borel for Borel S. Hence for Borel S the image of H^n⌞S under the measurable embedding η_{y,r} is r^n·H^n⌞η_{y,r}(S), and ∫_{η_{y,r}(S)} f dH^n = r^{-n}∫_S f(η_{y,r}(z)) dH^n(z) whenever either side is an integral of an integrable function (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, integral_smul_measure). (e) 0 ≤ J_F(a) ≤ L^n for every a, and J_F is Borel (SimonGMT measurable_areaJacobianAt): ‖DF(a)‖ ≤ L (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz; DF(a) = 0 where F is not differentiable), and normDet(T) ≤ ‖T‖^n for every linear T : ℝ^n → E, because normDet(T)·ω_n = H^n(T(B̄_1(0))) ≤ ‖T‖^n H^n(B̄_1(0)) = ‖T‖^n ω_n (Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and the Lipschitz image bound).
1. Countable compact cover. If U = ∅ then Y = ∅, so F(B) ⊆ ∅ forces B = ∅ and the claim is trivial (volume.restrict ∅ = 0); assume U ≠ ∅. U is open in the separable space E, so there are closed balls C_k = B̄_{s_k}(q_k) ⊆ U (k ∈ ℕ, s_k > 0) whose open balls B_{s_k}(q_k) cover U (centres in a countable dense set, positive rational radii, closures inside U). Each C_k is compact and ⊆ U, so H^n(Y ∩ C_k) < ∞.
2. Density of A in Y. Fix k and let ν_k := H^n⌞(Y ∩ C_k), a finite (hence locally finite) Borel measure (IsFiniteMeasure from H^n(Y ∩ C_k) < ∞, isFiniteMeasure_restrict). By the Besicovitch density theorem (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div applied to ν_k and A; E is finite-dimensional), for ν_k⌞A-a.e. y: ν_k(A ∩ B̄_r(y))/ν_k(B̄_r(y)) → 1 as r → 0⁺. Since A ⊆ Y and A, Y, C_k are Borel, ν_k⌞A = H^n⌞(A ∩ C_k), so this holds for H^n-a.e. y ∈ A ∩ C_k. Discarding the countable union N₁ of the exceptional sets (H^n(N₁) = 0), every y ∈ A ∖ N₁ is density-good: the convergence holds for every k with y ∈ C_k.
3. Smallness of Y ∖ A. Let y = F(b) (b ∈ B) be density-good and choose k with y ∈ B_{s_k}(q_k); put r₀ := s_k − |y − q_k| > 0. For 0 < r < r₀, B̄_r(y) ⊆ C_k, so with a(r) := H^n(A ∩ B̄_r(y)) and z(r) := H^n((Y ∖ A) ∩ B̄_r(y)) we get ν_k(A ∩ B̄_r(y)) = a(r) and ν_k(B̄_r(y)) = a(r) + z(r) < ∞; by step 2, a(r)/(a(r) + z(r)) → 1, so for each ε ∈ (0, 1/2) there is r_ε ∈ (0, r₀) with z(r) ≤ ε(a(r) + z(r)), hence z(r) ≤ 2ε a(r), for 0 < r < r_ε. If a ∈ B and F(a) ∈ B̄_r(y) then m|a − b| ≤ |F(a) − F(b)| ≤ r, so A ∩ B̄_r(y) ⊆ F(B ∩ B̄_{r/m}(b)) and, by 0(c), a(r) ≤ L^n λ(B̄_{r/m}(b)) = L^n ω_n m^{-n} r^n (this bound holds for every b ∈ B and r > 0). Thus z(r) ≤ 2ε L^n ω_n m^{-n} r^n for r < r_ε, i.e. r^{-n} z(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺.

By Lebesgue's density and differentiation theorems for λ on ℝ^n (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div for λ and B; IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub for λ, an additive Haar measure, and J_F, which is bounded and Borel, hence locally integrable), λ-a.e. b ∈ B satisfies (α) b is a density point of B: λ(B̄_ρ(b) ∖ B)/λ(B̄_ρ(b)) → 0 as ρ → 0⁺, and (β) b is a Lebesgue point of J_F: ρ^{-n} ∫_{B̄_ρ(b)} |J_F(a) − J_F(b)| dλ(a) → 0 as ρ → 0⁺ (= ω_n times the average). Every b ∈ B with (α) also satisfies (γ) |L_b c| ≥ m|c| for all c ∈ ℝ^n. Proof of (γ): it is trivial for c = 0; let c ≠ 0 (so n ≥ 1). There are r_l → 0⁺ and c_l → c with b + r_l c_l ∈ B: otherwise there are ε ∈ (0, |c|) and r₁ > 0 with B ∩ (b + r B_ε(c)) = ∅ for all r ∈ (0, r₁); but b + r B_ε(c) ⊆ B̄_{r(|c|+ε)}(b) has measure r^n λ(B_ε(0)) = (ε/(|c|+ε))^n λ(B̄_{r(|c|+ε)}(b)) (open and closed balls have the same Lebesgue measure, Measure.addHaar_closedBall_eq_addHaar_ball, which needs ℝ^n nontrivial: true since c ≠ 0; λ scales by r^n under dilation by r), a fixed positive fraction of λ(B̄_ρ(b)) for every ρ = r(|c|+ε) < r₁(|c|+ε), contradicting (α). Then m r_l|c_l| ≤ |F(b + r_l c_l) − F(b)| = |r_l L_b c_l + o(r_l)| (differentiability at b, |c_l| bounded); divide by r_l and let l → ∞ to get m|c| ≤ |L_b c|.
5. Blow-up of A. Let b ∈ B satisfy (α) and (β), y := F(b), f ∈ C_c(E) and R > 0 with f = 0 outside B_R(0). Put Φ_r(c) := (F(b + rc) − F(b))/r for r > 0, c ∈ ℝ^n.

By 0(d), the weighted area formula for the injective Lipschitz map F on B (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn, finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n, applied to the weights (f∘η_{y,r})⁺ and (f∘η_{y,r})⁻ and subtracted; all terms are finite since f is bounded and only B ∩ B̄_{rR/m}(b) contributes) and the substitution a = b + rc (λ scales by r^n): ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n = r^{-n}∫_B J_F(a) f((F(a) − y)/r) dλ(a) = ∫_{ℝ^n} 1_B(b + rc) J_F(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) dλ(c).

 (c) Convergence: for c ∈ D, |1_B(b + rc) J_F(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) − J_F(b) f(L_b c)| ≤ L^n‖f‖_∞ 1_{D ∖ r^{-1}(B − b)}(c) + ‖f‖_∞ |J_F(b + rc) − J_F(b)| + J_F(b)|f(Φ_r(c)) − f(L_b c)| (add and subtract J_F(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) and J_F(b) f(Φ_r(c)); 0(e)). Integrating over D: the first term gives L^n‖f‖_∞ r^{-n} λ(B̄_{rR/m}(b) ∖ B) → 0 by (α) (λ(B̄_{rR/m}(b)) = ω_n(R/m)^n r^n); the second gives ‖f‖_∞ r^{-n} ∫_{B̄_{rR/m}(b)} |J_F − J_F(b)| dλ → 0 by (β); the third is ≤ J_F(b) λ(D) sup_{c∈D} |f(Φ_r(c)) − f(L_b c)| → 0 because Φ_r → L_b uniformly on D (F is differentiable at b) and f is uniformly continuous. subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable with H^n(M ∩ C) < ∞ for every compact C ⊆ U, and φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P a C¹ map with Dφ(x) injective for every x, Λ-Lipschitz and Λ-antilipschitz, with φ^{-1}(U) = U. Source: step 6 of the parent proof. Simon 6.3.7 (chapter-06.txt lines 822–831) uses, without proof, that at H^n-a.e. point the approximate tangent space of f(M) is spanned by the images d^M f_x(τ_i); for the C¹ diffeomorphism φ this is supplied here from the siblings, with the details filled in. Notation: E := ℝ^P, H^n := μHE[n], λ := Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n (= μHE[n] there), Q(x) := approxTangentPlane n M x (by definition the chosen plane P with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x P when one exists, ⊥ otherwise). By the sibling dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces (M Borel, countably n-rectifiable) there are Lipschitz F_i (with constants L_i), Borel B_i ⊆ ℝ^n and m_i > 0 with m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i a − F_i a'| on B_i, F_i differentiable with injective derivative on B_i, P_i := F_i(B_i) Borel ⊆ M pairwise disjoint, and Z := M ∖ ⋃_i P_i H^n-null.

For such b the existential in the definition of approxTangentPlane holds, so HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M (F_i b) Q(F_i b) (Exists.choose_spec), and by uniqueness of approximate tangent planes (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique; Simon Ch. 3 1.5(1)) Q(F_i b) = range DF_i(b).
3. Properties of φ(M). φ is continuous and injective (antilipschitz), so φ(M) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn). Since φ^{-1}(U) = U, x ∈ M ⊆ U implies φ(x) ∈ U, so φ(M) ⊆ U. For compact C ⊆ U: φ^{-1}(C) is closed (φ continuous) and bounded (|x − x₀| ≤ Λ|φ(x) − φ(x₀)| for a fixed x₀), hence compact, and φ^{-1}(C) ⊆ φ^{-1}(U) = U; as φ(M) ∩ C ⊆ φ(M ∩ φ^{-1}(C)), H^n(φ(M) ∩ C) ≤ Λ^n H^n(M ∩ φ^{-1}(C)) < ∞ (LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le; μHE[n] is a fixed multiple of μH[n]).
4. Tangent planes of φ(M) along the pieces. Φ_i := φ∘F_i is (ΛL_i)-Lipschitz; for a, a' ∈ B_i, |Φ_i(a) − Φ_i(a')| ≥ Λ^{-1}|F_i(a) − F_i(a')| ≥ (m_i/Λ)|a − a'|; at b ∈ B_i, φ is differentiable at F_i(b) (φ is C¹) and F_i at b, so DΦ_i(b) = Dφ(F_i b)∘DF_i(b) (chain rule, fderiv_comp), which is injective as a composition of injective maps; Φ_i(B_i) ⊆ φ(M). Apply the sibling dpf_approxTangent_ae_bilipschitz_piece with Y := φ(M) (step 3) and (Φ_i, B_i, ΛL_i, m_i/Λ): for λ-a.e. b ∈ B_i, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n φ(M) (φ(F_i b)) (range(Dφ(F_i b)∘DF_i(b))), and range(Dφ(F_i b)∘DF_i(b)) = Dφ(F_i b)(range DF_i(b)) (LinearMap.range_comp, after ContinuousLinearMap.coe_comp).
5. Combination. By steps 2 and 4 there is a λ-null N_i ⊆ B_i such that for every b ∈ B_i ∖ N_i, x := F_i(b) satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q(x) and, since Q(x) = range DF_i(b), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n φ(M) φ(x) (Dφ(x)(Q(x))).
6. Transfer to x. Every x ∈ M at which the conclusion fails lies in Z ∪ ⋃_i F_i(N_i) (an x ∈ P_i has the form F_i(b) with b ∈ B_i, and b ∈ N_i if the conclusion fails at x). H^n(Z) = 0 and H^n(F_i(N_i)) ≤ L_i^n H^n(N_i) = L_i^n λ(N_i) = 0. So the exceptional set is H^n-null, i.e. the conclusion holds for μHE[n]⌞M-a.e. x. The density lemma with Y = M gives T_{F_i b}M = range DF_i(b) for a.e. b, hence Q(F_i b) = range DF_i(b) by uniqueness.
φ(M) is Borel, contained in U and locally H^n-finite (φ bi-Lipschitz, φ^{-1}(U) = U).
The density lemma with Y = φ(M) and pieces φ∘F_i gives T_{φF_i b}φ(M) = Dφ(F_i b)(range DF_i(b)) for a.e. b.
Lipschitz images of λ-null parameter sets are H^n-null, so both statements hold H^n-a.e. on M.

The chain rule identifies the image derivative range, uniqueness identifies the chosen original tangent plane, and Lipschitz null-image estimates transfer the conclusion from parameters to M. subproblem.title: Simon 6.3.6–3.9 for a bi-Lipschitz C¹ diffeomorphism: the image triple (φ(M), θ∘φ^{-1}, induced orientation)
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n), and φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P a C¹ bijection with Dφ(x) injective for every x, Λ-Lipschitz and Λ-antilipschitz, with φ^{-1}(U) = U, and assume x ↦ orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x is H^n⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable. Then there is an integer multiplicity triple R' in U with R'.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(φ(x))∘Dφ(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the parent proof; Simon 6.3.6–3.9 for injective f (chapter-06.txt lines 815–862: f_#T = τ(f(M), θ∘f^{-1}, η) with the induced orientation η of 3.5/3.7) and 6.2.24(3) (lines 426–440: for 1:1 f, f_#T(ω) = ∫_{f(M_+)} ⟨ω(y), η(y)⟩ dH^n by the area formula), with the details filled in. Notation: E := ℝ^P, H^n := μHE[n], μ := H^n⌞M, Q(x) := approxTangentPlane n M x, ψ := φ^{-1}; J(x) := sqrt(det(⟨Dφ(x)e_a, Dφ(x)e_b⟩)) with e = stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q(x) (the Jacobian of the siblings); ζ(x) := (R.orient x).comp (compContinuousLinearMapCLM (Dφ x)), i.e. ζ(x)(β) = ξ(x)(β∘Dφ(x)). Replacing Λ by max(Λ, 1) we assume Λ ≥ 1.
1. Facts on φ and ψ. ψ is Λ-Lipschitz (for y = φ(x), y' = φ(x'): |ψy − ψy'| = |x − x'| ≤ Λ|y − y'|), hence continuous and Borel measurable. φ(U) = U (φ^{-1}(U) = U and φ is surjective); for compact C ⊆ U, ψ(C) = φ^{-1}(C) is compact and ⊆ U. For every A ⊆ E, H^n(φ(A)) ≤ Λ^n H^n(A) and H^n(ψ(A)) ≤ Λ^n H^n(A) (LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le; μHE[n] is a fixed multiple of μH[n]). ‖Dφ(x)‖ ≤ Λ (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
2. Local finiteness of M. θ ≥ 1 on M (R.mult_pos), so H^n(M ∩ C) ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dH^n < ∞ for compact C ⊆ U (R.locallyIntegrable_mult).
3. Inputs. (G) By the sibling dpf_approxTangent_bilipschitz_image_ae (U open, M = R.carrier Borel ⊆ U, R.rectifiable, step 2, φ C¹ with injective derivatives, Λ-Lipschitz, Λ-antilipschitz, φ^{-1}(U) = U): for μ-a.e. x, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q(x) and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n φ(M) φ(x) (Dφ(x)Q(x)). (H) By the sibling dpf_area_formula_bilipschitz_rectifiable (φ injective): ∫⁻_{φ(M)} g dH^n = ∫⁻_M J(x) g(φ(x)) dH^n(x) for every g : E → [0, ∞]. (I) By the sibling dpf_aestronglyMeasurable_gramJacobian with μ, Q, L := Dφ (continuous, hence a.e. strongly measurable) and the projection hypothesis: J is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. (O) By R.orients: for μ-a.e. x there is Q' with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q' and IsUnitOrientationOf ξ(x) Q'.
 Let G ⊆ M be the set of x where (G) and (O) hold; H^n(M ∖ G) = 0. For x ∈ G, Q' = Q(x) by uniqueness (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so ξ(x) orients Q(x), and the sibling dpf_unitOrientation_map_gramNormalized (with ξ(x), Q(x), Dφ(x) injective, J = J(x)) gives 0 < J(x) ≤ ‖Dφ(x)‖^n ≤ Λ^n and IsUnitOrientationOf (J(x)^{-1} ζ(x)) (Dφ(x)Q(x)).
4. Definition of R'. Carrier M' := φ(M); multiplicity θ'(y) := θ(ψ(y)); orientation ξ'(y) := J(ψ(y))^{-1} • ζ(ψ(y)) (equal to 0 where J(ψ(y)) = 0, as 0^{-1} = 0).
5. The fields of IMRep. (a) M' = ψ^{-1}(M) (φ bijective) is Borel since ψ is continuous. (b) M' = φ(M) ⊆ φ(U) = U. (c) M' is countably n-rectifiable: if M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n) as in CountablyRectifiable, then M' ⊆ φ(M₀) ∪ ⋃_j (φ∘F_j)(ℝ^n), H^n(φ(M₀)) ≤ Λ^n · 0 = 0 and φ∘F_j is Lipschitz. (d) θ' = θ∘ψ is measurable. (e) For y ∈ M', ψ(y) ∈ M, so θ'(y) = θ(ψ(y)) > 0. (f) Local integrability: for compact C ⊆ U, apply (H) to g := 1_C θ' (note θ'(φ(x)) = θ(x) and 1_C(φ(x)) = 1_{ψ(C)}(x)): ∫⁻_{M'∩C} θ' dH^n = ∫⁻_M J(x) 1_{ψ(C)}(x) θ(x) dH^n(x) ≤ Λ^n ∫⁻_{M∩ψ(C)} θ dH^n < ∞, using J ≤ Λ^n μ-a.e. (step 3) and R.locallyIntegrable_mult for the compact ψ(C) ⊆ U. (g) ξ' is a.e. strongly measurable for μ' := H^n⌞M': the map f(x) := J(x)^{-1} • ζ(x) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (J by (I) and inversion on ℝ is measurable; ζ because ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient), Dφ is continuous and (ξ, L) ↦ ξ.comp (compContinuousLinearMapCLM L) is continuous, by ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM and continuity of composition). ψ is quasi-measure-preserving from μ' to μ: it is measurable, and for Borel A, μ'(ψ^{-1}(A)) = H^n(φ(M) ∩ φ(A)) = H^n(φ(M ∩ A)) ≤ Λ^n μ(A), so the image measure of μ' under ψ is absolutely continuous with respect to μ (it suffices to test measurable sets, Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.mk). Hence ξ' = f∘ψ is μ'-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_quasiMeasurePreserving). (h) Orientation: for y ∈ φ(G), x := ψ(y) ∈ G, and by step 3 ξ'(y) = J(x)^{-1} ζ(x) is a unit orientation of Dφ(x)Q(x), which is an approximate tangent plane of M' at y = φ(x) by (G). M' ∖ φ(G) = φ(M ∖ G) has H^n-measure ≤ Λ^n · 0 = 0, so this holds for μ'-a.e. y. Thus R' := (M', θ', ξ') is an IMRep U n.
6. The action. Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U); let h(y) := θ'(y) ξ'(y)(ω(y)) and g_ω(x) := θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(φ(x))∘Dφ(x)) = θ(x) ζ(x)(ω(φ(x))).
 (a) For x ∈ G: J(x) h(φ(x)) = J(x) θ(x) J(x)^{-1} ζ(x)(ω(φ(x))) = g_ω(x) since J(x) > 0 and ψ(φ(x)) = x. Since J ≥ 0, J·(h∘φ)⁺ = (g_ω)⁺, J·(h∘φ)⁻ = (g_ω)⁻ and J·|h∘φ| = |g_ω| μ-a.e. (positive and negative parts).
 (b) g_ω is μ-integrable: it is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable, x ↦ ω(φ(x))∘Dφ(x) continuous, evaluation continuous), and for μ-a.e. x, |g_ω(x)| ≤ θ(x)‖ω‖_∞ Λ^n 1_{ψ(tsupport ω)}(x) (|ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ because ξ(x) = ±evaluation at an orthonormal frame, by (O); ‖β∘L‖ ≤ ‖β‖‖L‖^n; ω(φ(x)) = 0 unless x ∈ ψ(tsupport ω), a compact subset of U), which is integrable by R.locallyIntegrable_mult.
 (c) h is μ'-integrable: it is μ'-a.e. strongly measurable (θ' measurable, ξ' a.e. strongly measurable by 5(g), ω continuous, evaluation continuous), and by (H) with g := ‖h‖₊ and (a), ∫⁻_{M'} |h| dH^n = ∫⁻_M J |h∘φ| dH^n = ∫⁻_M |g_ω| dH^n < ∞ by (b).
 (d) By (H) applied to g := ofReal(h⁺) and to g := ofReal(h⁻), and (a): ∫⁻_{M'} h^± dH^n = ∫⁻_M J (h∘φ)^± dH^n = ∫⁻_M (g_ω)^± dH^n. For integrable real functions ∫ f = ∫⁻ f⁺ − ∫⁻ f⁻ (integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part), so R'.action(ω) = ∫_{M'} h dH^n = ∫_M g_ω dH^n = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(φ(x))∘Dφ(x)) dH^n(x).
7. Dimension zero needs no change: for n = 0, Q(x) = {0}, J = 1, β∘Dφ(x) = β for 0-covectors, so ζ = ξ and ξ' = ξ∘ψ.
